title: Pack the bag (0/1 knapsack)
prompt:
Item i has weight weights[i] and value values[i]. Each item can be packed at most once. Return the largest total value whose total weight is at most capacity.

- 0 to 200 items; weights between 1 and 1,000; values between 0 and 10^6; 0 <= capacity <= 10,000.
hints: For each item you either take it or skip it. Trying every subset is 2^n.
Let best[c] be the best value using capacity c with the items considered so far.
For each item, update c from capacity down to its weight: best[c] = max(best[c], best[c - w] + v). Going downward stops an item being used twice.

solution.explanation: The 2D table best[i][c] (first i items, capacity c) compresses to one row. Iterating capacity downward means best[c - w] still refers to the row before this item, so each item is used at most once. Iterating upward would give the unbounded knapsack.

complexity.notes: This is pseudo-polynomial: it is polynomial in the numeric value of capacity, not in its number of bits. 0/1 knapsack is NP-hard in general.

followUps: Which items were chosen? What extra state do you need to reconstruct them?
